headline: Evening Wrap: Tech Sell-Off Continues, NVDA -5% Despite Blowout
body:
Markets closed lower for a second consecutive day on Thursday as tech stocks sold off despite Nvidia's stellar Q4 results. The Dow managed a modest +0.4% gain on defensive rotation, but the S&P 500 slipped -0.54% to 6,908.86 and the Nasdaq fell -1.18% to 22,878.38. The action reflects a classic "sell the news" pattern and growing concerns about AI valuations ahead of tomorrow's inflation data (PPI).

Key Movers:
- NVDA: -5% close despite $1.62 EPS, $68.1B revenue
- DELL: +2% regular, +3% AH on AI server strength
- CRWV: +8% AH on $12.025B 2026 revenue guide
- STLA: -5% confirming $26B annual loss
- TTD: -16.8% on weak guidance

headline: January PPI (8:30 AM) - Key Inflation Gauge to Set Tone
body:
Tomorrow morning's January Producer Price Index will be the first major economic data point that could sway the market's direction. Expectations: +0.3% m/m, +3.2% y/y.

Scenarios:
• Hot (>0.4%) — Bad for tech, could accelerate rate hike fears, equities sell
• Cool (<0.2%) — Relief rally in tech and growth names likely
• In-line — market may grind sideways

This is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge (alongside CPI). Hot PPI = higher yields = pressure on high-PE stocks. Light PPI = short-covering rally possible. Watch EUR/USD and 10-Year yield reaction for clues.

headline: Snowflake Earnings After-Close - High Volatility Setup
body:
Snowflake (SNOW) reports Q4 earnings after market close tomorrow. Expectations: loss $0.58, revenue $1.89B.

Why it matters:
- Cloud spending health check for 2026
- AI/data warehouse narrative barometer
- High short interest (~15%) → potential short squeeze on any good news
- Options implied move ~10% both ways

Past quarters have triggered major moves (up 15% on good news, down 20% on weak). High IV straddle suggests options are pricing a big move. Likely sets tone for cloud/software sector next week.

headline: SPY Put Wall at $690 - Critical Support Test Tomorrow
body:
SPY is trading just above a massive $3.3 billion put wall at $690 according to options data. This concentration of put options acts as both resistance (if market tries to rally) and support (if sellers need to hedge or roll).

Bulls want: Hold above $690 into PPI
Bears want: Push below $690 to trigger gamma hedging
Bias: Range-bound until PPI breaks the pattern

If SPY breaks $690: quick drop to 685-680 likely
If SPY holds $690 and PPI is good: short-cover to 695-700
Tomorrow's PPI is likely the catalyst to string this range.
